articleTitle: Direction-specific effects of balance training on dynamic balance in athletes with chronic ankle instability: a multilevel meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
takeaways: Balance training specifically improves dynamic balance performance in athletes with chronic ankle instability, with effects varying by training direction and assessment method used
Athletes with chronic ankle instability who underwent balance training interventions showed measurable improvements in dynamic balance tests compared to control groups or alternative treatments

The effectiveness of balance training for chronic ankle instability depends on specific participant characteristics, suggesting personalized approaches may be more beneficial than one-size-fits-all protocols
Different types of balance training modalities produced varying levels of improvement in dynamic balance, indicating that training specificity matters for optimal outcomes in ankle rehabilitation
